prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
competitors_mentioned: Check the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC)
answer_verbatim:
I can’t point to one single “best” company for everyone — the best choice depends on your exact location, system make/age, urgency, budget and whether you want a local independent or a national franchise. If you tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood, whether this is an emergency, and the make/age of the unit (if known), I can give specific, nearby recommendations. Meanwhile, here’s how to find the right HVAC company in Phoenix and what to watch for.

What to do now (quick)
- If it’s an emergency (no cooling and temps are dangerous), ask for a company that offers 24/7 emergency service and same‑day dispatch. Provide your ZIP so I can suggest candidates.
- Otherwise, get 2–3 estimates before agreeing to major repairs or replacement.

How to find reputable local companies
- Search for “AC repair Phoenix [your ZIP]” and sort by Google/Yelp reviews. Give more weight to companies with many recent positive reviews.
- Check the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) to confirm the contractor’s license and any disciplinary history.
- Look at Better Business Bureau (BBB) rating and complaint history.
- Prefer companies that are licensed, insured, and (if relevant) factory‑authorized for your brand (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.).

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your ROC license number?
- Do you offer a written diagnostic and written estimate?
- Is the quote flat rate or hourly? What is the diagnostic fee?
- Do you provide a parts/labor warranty? How long?
- Are you available for emergency or same‑day service?
- Can you provide recent local references or online reviews?

Red flags to avoid
- Technicians who pressure you into a full system replacement without showing diagnostics.
- Unmarked vehicles or technicians who can’t provide a company name or license.
- “Too good to be true” ultra-low quotes without written scope.
- Requests for large cash payment up front with no invoice or contract.

Typical cost ranges (Phoenix, approximate)
- Diagnostic visit: $75–$150
- Simple repairs (capacitor/contactor): $100–$400
- Refrigerant recharge (if legal and minor): $150–$450
- Major parts (compressor, condenser): $1,200–$4,000 depending on unit and labor
(These vary widely — get written estimates.)

If you want, I can:
- Recommend several specific, highly‑rated HVAC companies near you if you share your ZIP or neighborhood.
- Help you script the phone call or compare 2–3 written estimates you receive.

Which would you like to do?
